topic: Spousal RRSP: higher earner contributes and deducts from own room; spouse withdraws later at a lower rate; 3-year attribution (premiums in the year or two preceding years) taxes early withdrawals to the contributor

example.note: example (not a CRA rule): Manitoba couple, taxable incomes $120,000 (Alex) and $30,000 (Sam), 2026 federal + Manitoba brackets; Sam's withdrawal tax uses 2026 rates as an illustration of a future year; credits unchanged at these incomes; pension income splitting, OAS clawback and future rate changes not modelled. Computed by d4/calc.py.

spoken.saving_round: three thousand nine hundred and fifty dollars
spoken.sam_round: two thousand four hundred and eighty dollars
spoken.early_round: four thousand three hundred and forty dollars

sources.deduction: ITA 146(5.1): premiums paid to a spousal or common-law partner RRSP are deductible by the contributor, limited by the contributor's own RRSP deduction limit (146(5.1)(b)); payable up to 60 days after year-end; laws.justice.gc.ca current to 2026-09-30
sources.attribution: ITA 146(8.3): a withdrawal by the spouse is included in the contributor's income up to premiums paid by the contributor to a spousal plan in the year or in one of the two immediately preceding taxation years (not if living separate and apart due to breakdown)
sources.not_covered: pension income splitting (next video), RRIF minimum-amount exception to attribution, marriage breakdown exception named only in the bible
